chief_complaint: excessive glandular breast tissue in young male, embarrassed
hpi_details: A 19-year-old male presents with bilateral excessive glandular breast tissue and embarrassment. The enlargement developed gradually, and he denies nipple discharge or a focal hard mass.
ideas: He thinks the chest swelling is due to leftover puberty hormones or drinking too many energy drinks.
concerns: He is worried that classmates will notice his chest and mock him, preventing him from going to the campus pool or gym.
expectations: He hopes the doctor can prescribe pills to shrink the tissue or refer him to a surgeon to flatten his chest.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Reconstructive Gynecomastia is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Plan for Reconstructive Gynecomastia: Endocrine workup, elective surgical excision (subcutaneous mastectomy), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: excessive glandular breast tissue in young male, embarrassed
Key HPI features: A 19-year-old male presents with gradually developing bilateral glandular breast enlargement and embarrassment.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Reconstructive Gynecomastia.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Reconstructive Gynecomastia.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Proceeding to elective surgery before excluding medication-related, endocrine, testicular, or malignant causes.
management_principles: Plan for Reconstructive Gynecomastia: Endocrine workup, elective surgical excision (subcutaneous mastectomy)
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

must_ask.say: When did you first notice the breast enlargement, and has it been getting bigger?
Have you noticed any discharge from the nipple or a hard lump?
Are you taking any medications, supplements, or using anabolic steroids or marijuana?
Is it on both sides equally, and is it tender to touch?
How has this affected you emotionally or socially?

history.answer: Doctor, my chest has grown large like a woman's breasts over the past year, and it is making me feel really embarrassed.
I first started noticing the puffiness about a year ago when my tighter shirts started fitting awkwardly across my chest.
It is on both sides right behind the nipples, forming round, rubbery swelling about two or three inches across.
It has grown slowly and steadily over the past year, but it has not had any sudden growth spurts.
No, there is no pain at all, and it does not hurt even when I press on it or when clothes rub against it.
No, the skin looks completely smooth with no dimpling, redness, or puckering, and my nipples are not pulled inward.
No, I have never had any fluid, milk, or blood come out of either nipple.
No, I have not felt any lumps or swollen glands under my armpits or around my collarbone.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, redness, or heat in my chest.
No, my weight has been steady at around seventy kilograms, and my appetite is completely normal.
No, I do not have any bone pain, chronic cough, shortness of breath, or headache.
No, I have never had an injury to my chest or any surgery or procedures done there.
No, I have never had any breast conditions, biopsies, or radiation therapy to my chest.
No, I have never taken anabolic steroids, testosterone, bodybuilding powders, or protein supplements.
No, I have never taken hormone pills, prostate medications, ulcer drugs, or psychiatric medications.
No, I have not noticed any lumps, swelling, or shrinking in my testicles, and my sex drive is completely normal.
No, I have never had yellow skin or eyes, abdominal swelling, or any history of liver disease.
It has really hurt my confidence; I avoid taking my shirt off at the gym or pool, and I always wear baggy, dark t-shirts to hide it.
I figured my hormones from puberty might still be out of balance, or maybe it was caused by drinking too many energy drinks.
I'm dreading going to the gym or locker room because I'm terrified people will notice and make fun of my chest.
I'm hoping you can prescribe medication to shrink the chest tissue or refer me to someone who can surgically remove it.
I have always been healthy and do not have high blood pressure, diabetes, thyroid disease, or any chronic conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I am not taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, herbal supplements, or vitamins.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes, vaped, or used marijuana.
I only have an occasional beer with friends once or twice a month, maybe one can at a time.
I am a nineteen-year-old college student, and I live in a dormitory on campus.
No one in my family has ever had breast cancer, ovarian cancer, or any other male breast problems.
My parents are both healthy, and there are no endocrine or hormone disorders in my family.
I am sexually active with one female partner, and I have not had any problems with sexual function or fertility.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.7 degrees Celsius, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, well-nourished young male in no acute distress with noticeable bilateral breast prominence beneath his shirt.
Symmetric bilateral breast enlargement with normal overlying skin; no erythema, dimpling, peau d orange, or nipple retraction with arms raised or hands on hips.
Firm, mobile, rubbery disc of glandular tissue palpated bilaterally beneath the areolae; no discrete hard or fixed nodules, no tenderness, and no nipple discharge on gentle expression.
No palpable axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy bilaterally.
Normal adult male external genitalia with both testes descended, symmetrical, normal in volume, and without masses, nodules, or tenderness.
No jaundice, spider angiomas, palmar erythema, or unusual skin lesions.
Soft, non-tender abdomen; liver and spleen are not palpable below the costal margins.
